Omar has one commit he hasn't pushed yet, adding VAT to the checkout total. Before stand-up he runs
"just to download what the team pushed". The terminal answers with
, the file is full of conflict markers, and his branch is in the middle of a merge he never asked for. He wanted to look. Git changed his branch.
downloads the latest changes from the remote. It's the opposite of
, the command that gets you "up to date", and it's safe to run any time.

It's a reasonable belief. The names suggest a pair: push uploads, so pull must download. And most of the time you pull with no commits of your own, where it really does look like a download. In our test, a clone with nothing new printed
That's the half-truth. A pull always starts with a download, but it never stops there. The second half only goes unnoticed while your branch has nothing new of its own.
Your clone keeps bookmarks of the remote
Your repository doesn't read the remote's branches live. It keeps a local copy of where they were, called
. Pro Git describes them as "local references that you can't move; Git moves them for you whenever you do any network communication." Your own
are two different pointers, and they can point at different commits.
downloads the commits you don't have yet and moves the bookmarks, so
now matches the remote. Your branches stay where they were, and Pro Git says fetch "will not modify your working directory at all." Afterwards you can compare
git pull adds an integration step

docs describe two steps: "First, git pull runs git fetch with the same arguments", then it picks the branch to integrate, by default the upstream of your current branch, and "integrates that branch into the current branch." That second step has several modes. A
moves your branch ahead when you have no commits of your own.

settings choose for you. When your branch and the remote have diverged and nothing chooses, the docs say pull does "fast-forward" updates only and "fails if your local branch has diverged". In our test, a diverged pull with no settings stopped with
fatal: Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches.
Which mode you get depends on configuration
Omar's pull merged because something had chosen for him. On our Windows test machine,

The fix: download first, then decide
Here are both sessions from Omar's clone, run on Git 2.54:

tabs.label: ❌ Wrong
tabs.code:
git pull   # "just download what the team pushed"
# From ../shop
#    f3f6d28..85d5919  main       -> origin/main
# Auto-merging checkout.js
# CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in checkout.js
# Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.
git status --short
# UU checkout.js

tabs.label: ✅ Right
tabs.code:
git fetch   # download only: moves origin/main, nothing else
# From ../shop
#    f3f6d28..85d5919  main       -> origin/main
git status -sb
# ## main...origin/main [ahead 1, behind 1]
git log --oneline main..origin/main   # what they pushed
# 85d5919 Add shipping to total
git diff --stat main...origin/main
#  checkout.js | 2 +-
#  1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

content.text: The first line of each output is identical: both commands downloaded the same commit and moved

content.text: In our opinion the safest everyday setting is
only ever fast-forwards: when you're simply behind, it updates you; when you've diverged, it fetches and stops with
fatal: Not possible to fast-forward, aborting.
The decision to merge or rebase stays with you, made when you're ready.

blocks.title: A pull that stops halfway leaves you mid-merge

content.text: After a conflicting pull, your branch is in the middle of a merge and the conflicted files contain markers. If that's not the moment to resolve it, the
